app.title: DockForgeAI — docking validation, screening and hit-prioritization dashboard
app.summary: A person first checks which stages of a precomputed docking pipeline have finished. Next they confirm that redocking reproduces the reference crystal pose: they read each pose's score and its RMSD against a pass threshold. They then look at the predicted protein–ligand contacts for one pose at a time, read the screening funnel and the docking scores, and open the consensus-ranked hit list to see one compound's full profile. The 3D view shows the receptor with each pose. At the end the person generates PDF/HTML reports and downloads the tables, figures and zipped bundles.

task.text: Check that a docking setup reproduces a known binding pose, then review screened compounds and pick which to prioritise from a consensus ranking.

data.text: Precomputed pipeline outputs: a table of docked poses with scores and RMSD, a table of protein–ligand contact records, a table of screening scores, a consensus-ranking table with descriptor and alert columns, receptor and pose structure files, and report summaries in JSON and Markdown.
data.item: a candidate compound docked into a target protein, with its score, contacts, descriptors and consensus rank

stage.text: confirming a docking setup and deciding which screened hits to prioritise, after the pipeline has run and before experimental follow-up

mechanism.text: Pages in a sidebar each show one pipeline stage as metric tiles over tabs that hold a bar or line chart, a filterable table and the raw report, and each has its own download buttons. Pose and compound selectors narrow the contact tables, open a per-compound profile and switch the 3D structure view. An export page regenerates the reports and bundles every output into zips.

field.text: structure-based virtual screening and molecular docking in computational drug discovery

workflow.name: validate a computational method on a known case, then rank candidates and package the evidence

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: Home shows a status card for each pipeline stage (ligand and receptor preparation, redocking, interactions, screening, tests). Each card shows whether that stage's output file exists.

steps.step: check the method against a known reference before trusting it
steps.here: Redocking metrics show the best affinity, the minimum RMSD and a validation verdict. Below them are a pose table marked PASS/FAIL against the 2 Å threshold, a bar chart of affinity per pose and a line chart of RMSD with the threshold drawn.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: A pose selector (crystallographic, rank‑1, best‑RMSD) filters the contact records. Counts appear for contact types, hydrogen bonds and catalytic-residue contacts, with charts by type and by top residue. A tab lists only the catalytic-site rows.
Screening shows the funnel from library to accepted, rejected, screened and refined as metrics and a bar chart. Below are the top docking scores and the full score table.

The consensus ranking table and bar chart lead to a compound selector. It opens a profile of consensus score, affinity, QED, ligand efficiency, interaction score, PAINS and Brenk alerts, and the SMILES.

Reports & Exports runs the report script to make PDF/HTML reports. It offers per-file downloads of reports, tables, summaries and molecule images, a zip of the figures and a zip of all outputs, and the manifest is shown.

distinctive: Trust in the method rests on a reference case: the redocked pose must come within an RMSD threshold of the crystal pose, and both top-ranked and best poses are judged.
Contacts with named catalytic residues are counted and listed apart from all other contacts.
The hit ranking combines several kinds of evidence (docking score, interactions, drug-likeness, structural alerts, ligand efficiency) into one consensus score.
The pages read outputs that have already been computed. Report generation never reruns the expensive docking, and every page warns that scores are not experimental binding evidence.

parts.title: Workflow status
parts.summary: Shows a card for each pipeline stage that says whether its output exists, plus the reference case being validated.

parts.title: Redocking validation
parts.summary: Compares docked poses with the crystal pose by affinity and RMSD, marks each pass or fail against the threshold, and offers the summary and the pose table for download.

parts.title: Protein–ligand interaction analysis
parts.summary: Filters predicted contacts by pose and shows counts, charts by interaction type and by residue, a catalytic-site table and the full records.

parts.title: Virtual screening
parts.summary: Shows how many library compounds were accepted, rejected, screened and refined, with a chart of the top docking scores and the full score table to download.

parts.title: Hit prioritization
parts.summary: Shows the consensus-ranked compounds as top-hit metrics, a table and a bar chart of consensus scores, with the ranking and the reports to download.

parts.title: Selected-hit profile
parts.summary: Opens one chosen compound's consensus score, affinity, drug-likeness, ligand efficiency, interaction score, structural alerts and SMILES.

parts.title: Interactive 3D protein–ligand viewer
parts.summary: Shows the receptor as a cartoon with the chosen pose (crystal, rank‑1 or best‑RMSD) as sticks and the catalytic residues highlighted; drag to rotate, scroll to zoom.
